To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
cyber warfare is a subset of cyber war.

• Cyber war and cyber warfare are used interchangeably in the literature; • The most common definitional origin of these terms is military doctrine; • The most commonly used definitions are from military doctrine; • Definitions of cyber war and warfare are more often used by military authors; • Definitions are used most frequently in academic journals and books; and • Definitions of cyber warfare are more often found in academic journals

the definitions of cyber war and warfare are not static, that they have been in a state of flux since the early 2000s, that they are still evolving, that they are being defined by a variety of actors, and that the definitions are becoming increasingly more nuanced as they are being refined.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: What are the definitional origins of cyber war and warfare? What patterns of usage emerge from the analysis? How do these definitions change over time and why?

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

‘Cyber War’ is a term used to describe a conflict between two or more nations that is conducted using cyber weapons, cyber warfare, cyber terrorism, or cyber crime to achieve a strategic or tactical advantage.
cyberwar is a form of warfare in which the actions and effects are conducted and achieved through cyberspace.
cyber war and cyber war‐fare are not the same, but they are related.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the definition of cyber war has evolved from a narrow focus on the use of cyber weapons in military conflicts to a broader focus on cyber attacks that can cause harm to a society, including those that are not military in nature.

The main takeaway from our work is that
cyber war and cyber war‐ fare are terms used to describe the same phenomenon.
